html:
A Korean admiral of the Joseon navy who won a string of sea battles against Japan in the Imjin War of 1592 to 1598. Koreans honour him as their greatest national hero.

In 1592 Toyotomi Hideyoshi sent a huge army into Korea, and it swept north to Pyongyang. At sea Yi, commander of a fleet in the southwest, struck back. He won at Okpo and then, in a crane wing formation, crushed a Japanese fleet at Hansan Island. His victories cut the sea route the Japanese needed to supply their armies.

He used a few turtle ships, armoured with a covered deck and spikes and armed with cannon, alongside sturdy Korean battleships.

Court rivals had him arrested and tortured in 1597. His successor then lost almost the whole fleet. Restored to command, Yi beat a far larger Japanese force at Myeongnyang with about thirteen ships. In December 1598, as the Japanese withdrew, he was shot and killed at the battle of Noryang. His war diary survives.
